note: Clean-room, Sentinel-authored from CWE-259/798. Bandit flags any credential-looking literal; many are placeholders/defaults/tests.
questions: Is the flagged literal an ACTUAL secret (password, API key, token, private key) rather than a placeholder, example, default, empty, or non-secret constant?
Is this literal used to authenticate or authorize against a REAL system (not a fixture, test, or local-dev-only value)?
Would disclosure of this literal grant real access to a protected resource?
keep_if: a real credential is hardcoded and used for real authentication/authorization
